title: A Puzzle Evening
story: Sofia cleared the low table and opened a box of puzzle pieces. Her friend Mateo had brought the puzzle to her flat. The picture on the lid showed a red boat on a blue lake. They turned every piece face up before they began. Sofia started with the border because the straight edges were easier to see. Mateo looked for corners and passed her four of them. The frame grew slowly around the lake. After an hour a gap remained near the boat. They searched the box, the floor, and both chairs. The missing piece was not in any of those places. Sofia sat back and tried to stay patient. Mateo lifted a sofa cushion and found the piece under it. He pressed it into the gap, and the boat was whole. They still had the sky to finish. The pale pieces looked almost the same, so they sorted them by shade. Bit by bit the clouds took shape. At nine the puzzle was complete. Sofia slid a board under it so they could move it safely. Mateo took a photo, and they left the puzzle on the table overnight. Sofia made tea, and they talked about a harder puzzle next month. She felt tired, but the finished lake made the room feel calm. Working side by side had been better than hunting for pieces alone.
